subject: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@acme.com>, Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed handoff so we can get the qualification runs scheduled: 

Key SLO targets you mentioned on the call:
- P95 latency (generation-only): <= 250 ms target, 350 ms fall-back SLA
- Sustained throughput: 180–220 RPS (90% of traffic in short queries)
- Concurrency: support 80 active sessions with KV cache retained per session
- Streaming: chunked deltas with first-token < 100 ms for interactive sessions; server-side keepalive 30s

What we need from Acme to reproduce and benchmark your workload:
1) Prompt set (representative sample): single-turn + streaming chat slices, anonymized — ideally as JSONL (one prompt per line).
2) Expected model variants to exercise (fp16 / 8-bit quant / natively quantized weights).
3) Typical sequence-length distribution and tokenization settings (we can infer but better to have exact).
4) Any special end-of-stream behavior (partial-delta acceptance, stop-token rules).

Deliverables Redwood will provide to run a reproducible qualification:
- Repo access: benchmark harness with Docker images and exact kernel flags (link below).
- Measurement definitions: p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, token-per-second accounting, and streaming-first-byte timing spec.
- Runbook: steps to spin up infra, seed KV cache, and replay prompt bundle deterministically.
- Baseline artifacts: suggested batch sizes and quantization profile recommendations for the 4090/MI300 targets you mentioned.

Next steps / actionable items:
- Alice: share a 200–500 prompt sample (anonymized), plus the model variants you want tested (reply with the file or Drive link).
- Connor / Marissa: we will prepare a reproducibility runbook and a short checklist; aim to request a 2-week window where Acme can allow us to run baseline reproductions in a staging slot.
- Bob: confirm the evaluation window dates and which internal stakeholders should be CC'd on the run results.

Attachments: placeholder for sample prompt schema and SLO matrix (I attached a template).

Repo / docs links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/kim/ACME-4527, https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-acme-playbook

Thanks — kim

--
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187


-----Original Message-----
From: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)

Thanks Kimberly — that summary is great and aligns with our internal notes. A couple clarifications before we share prompt samples: 

- For 'concurrency' we actually mean 80 active user sessions, each session maintaining a 2–3 message KV cache. Does your runbook seed per-session KV or do you replay fresh interactions?
- For streaming-first-byte target, 100 ms is aggressive for our current customer-facing UI; can you show how you measure 'first-token' for streaming? Is that from connection TCP/TLS handshake or from request arrival?

We'll drop an anonymized 300-prompt JSONL by EOD tomorrow. We'll also include 3 golden threads (longer multi-turn) to exercise KV cache behavior. Attaching our prompt export (sample) — filename: acme_prompt_samples_v1.jsonl (attached).

Best,
Alice

--
Alice Zhou
Senior Product Manager, Search & AI | Acme Retail
alice.zhou@acme.com | (212) 555-2190


From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@acme.com>, Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)

Perfect — thanks for the sample. Quick answers: 

- We seed per-session KV when you provide the golden threads. The harness supports two modes: cold-start replay (no KV) and warm-start (prepopulated KV via a seed file). We'll run both to match production and to characterize warm-cache gains.
- Streaming first-byte: our measurement is request-arrival (server received request headers) to first payload byte emitted by the model. That excludes TCP/TLS setup time (we assume persistent connections for benchmarking). We'll attach the timing spec to make it explicit (see repro_instructions_ACME-4527.md).

Attached: repro_instructions_ACME-4527.md, and a filled SLO template (slo_matrix_acme.xlsx).

Action: Connor — can you confirm the test infra (GPU family and instance size) you'd recommend? My initial read is to run 2 x A100-80GB for baseline fp16 and 4 x the 4090-class nodes for quantized variants.

Kim

--
From: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@acme.com>, Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)

Kim / team — noted. For reproducibility we should capture exact kernel versions and NV driver versions in the run artifacts. Proposed infra plan: 
- Baseline: 2 x A100-80GB (fp16) 
- Cost/throughput variants: 4 x RTX4090 nodes using our 8-bit quantized path (we'll pin the same container images)
- Single-node streaming stress: 1 x MI300 for concurrency stress test

I'll create a short infra sheet and a commit in the harness repo listing container tags and kernel/driver pins. Marissa, can you own the orchestration steps and the replay job?

Connor

--
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@acme.com>, Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook & reproducibility handoff for performance qual (Acme)

Connor — will do. I created a ticket and scheduled a 2-week reproducibility window starting Nov 15 (Nov 15–28) in our staging pool. Items I'll deliver before the window: 
- Orchestration checklist + exact container tags
- Warm-start seed process and verification script
- Run matrix (which prompts, model variants, and metrics to capture per run)

Alice / Bob — does Nov 15–28 work for your side for a reproducible run? If so, we'll block the slot and share run artifacts (logs, timing traces, kernel/driver metadata) to the Drive link.

Marissa

--
From: Bob Tran <bob.tran@acme.com>

Thanks team — Nov 15–28 works. We'll: 
- Deliver the full 3k prompt bundle and the 3 golden threads by Nov 10.
- Confirm model variants (we want baseline fp16 and the 8-bit quantized path).
- Provide a stakeholder list for run results distribution (PM, infra, and product ops).

Please proceed with the orchestration checklist and share the Drive link when ready. Looking forward to the reproducible artifacts — important for our procurement sign-off.

Best,
Bob
